sectors.note:
**TL;DR:** Energy continues its dominant run as the top-performing US sector, while defensive and cyclical laggards like Utilities and Industrials lose further ground.

The US equity market exhibits a narrow leadership profile, with only 3 of 11 sectors maintaining all-green status (positive across weekly, monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, and YTD horizons). Energy remains the undisputed leader, holding the number one YTD rank with an exceptional momentum score of 0.933 and demonstrating sustained strength across 1, 3, and 6-month periods. Healthcare and Financials are also rotating higher, both gaining one spot in rank over the last five sessions to secure their all-green status with momentum scores of 0.733 and 0.700, respectively.

Conversely, rate-sensitive and industrial sectors are fading. Industrials, Real Estate, and Utilities all dropped one spot in the rankings over the last five sessions. Utilities sits near the bottom of the momentum spectrum at 0.183, while Consumer Cyclical remains the lowest-ranked sector overall (rank 11) with a weak momentum score of 0.250.

## Strength
* **All-Green Breadth:** Only 3 of 11 sectors—Energy (0.933 momentum), Healthcare (0.733 momentum), and Financials (0.700 momentum)—are positive across all measured timeframes.
* **Energy Dominance:** Energy is the sole sector classified as "sustained strong," holding the rank 1 spot YTD with a momentum score of 0.933.
* **Healthcare & Financials Solidifying:** Both sectors are in the top three for momentum (0.733 and 0.700, respectively), reinforcing their all-green status.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Top Gainers:** Communication Services (rank 9, momentum 0.40), Financials (rank 6, momentum 0.70), and Healthcare (rank 4, momentum 0.73) each improved their rankings by +1 spot over the last five sessions.
* **Top Losers:** Industrials (rank 5, momentum 0.25), Real Estate (rank 7, momentum 0.33), and Utilities (rank 10, momentum 0.18) each slipped -1 spot in the last five sessions.
* **Momentum Chasm:** A wide gap persists between leaders like Technology (0.667 momentum, rank 2) and laggards like Consumer Cyclical (0.250 momentum, rank 11) and Utilities (0.183 momentum, rank 10).

## Divergences
* **No Fragile All-Green Signals:** There are no early-warning divergences or fragile all-green sectors detected in the current data, indicating stable alignment for the leading groups.
* **Consistent Leadership:** The top-ranked sectors (Energy, Technology, and Basic Materials) show no rank-to-momentum mismatches or negative divergence signals.

industries.note:
**TL;DR:** Energy and marine shipping dominate absolute market strength with near-perfect momentum, while defensive sectors like medical distribution and water utilities rotate upward as clean energy and metals fade.

US industry breadth remains highly concentrated, with only 16 of 144 groups (11.1%) achieving "all-green" status across all time horizons. Absolute leadership is anchored firmly in the energy and shipping sectors, led by Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (0.991 momentum) and Marine Shipping (0.911 momentum). Meanwhile, a defensive rotation is emerging, evidenced by sharp weekly rank improvements in Medical Distribution (+22 spots to rank 57) and Utilities - Regulated Water (+19 spots to rank 62).

Conversely, clean energy and commodity-linked groups are experiencing a sharp pullback. Uranium plummeted 21 spots to rank 75, and Utilities - Renewable fell 18 spots to rank 105. Momentum is also beginning to fracture in previously resilient commodity groups, with Coking Coal, Copper, and Gold all experiencing notable rank declines over the last five sessions despite their high absolute momentum scores.

## Strength
* **Energy Leadership:** Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing leads all groups with a momentum score of 0.991, supported by Oil & Gas Integrated (0.857) and Oil & Gas E&P (0.81), all of which maintain perfect "all-green" status.
* **Sustained Outperformance:** Marine Shipping (momentum 0.911) and Agricultural Inputs (momentum 0.851) continue to show long-term institutional backing, remaining in the top 36 across 1-, 3-, and 6-month horizons.
* **Financial & Defensive Anchors:** Banks - Diversified (momentum 0.84) and Insurance - Reinsurance (momentum 0.83) remain highly stable, anchoring the 16 fully aligned "all-green" industry groups.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Top Weekly Gainers:** Medical Distribution surged 22 spots to rank 57 (momentum 0.77), while Utilities - Regulated Water gained 19 spots to rank 62 (momentum 0.67) and Discount Stores climbed 18 spots to rank 87 (momentum 0.44).
* **Steepest Declines:** Uranium fell 21 spots to rank 75 (momentum 0.36), followed closely by Utilities - Renewable, which dropped 18 spots to rank 105 (momentum 0.23).
* **Momentum Extremes:** Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (0.991) and Marine Shipping (0.911) represent the strongest momentum profiles in the market, while Advertising Agencies (0.113) and Footwear & Accessories (0.101) remain anchored at the bottom.

## Divergences
* **Fading Commodities:** High-momentum groups are showing early signs of exhaustion, led by Coking Coal (momentum 0.62, down 11 spots), Gold (momentum 0.69, down 8 spots), and Copper (momentum 0.67, down 8 spots).
* **Emerging Value:** Discount Stores (up 18 spots, momentum 0.44) and Aluminum (up 7 spots, momentum 0.50) are climbing in rank despite relatively low absolute momentum scores, indicating early-stage accumulation.
* **Defensive Consolidation:** Diagnostics & Research is showing minor distribution, slipping 3 spots to a momentum score of 0.70, even as it remains in the "sustained strong" category.
